doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Dunbar High School band, the cello that failed and the viola
summary: At Dunbar she wanted cello but could not play it in a skirt, so played viola for about two years.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And did you . . . well, I guess you did the same thing there. You played a great deal. Did you play in the band, or any formal musical activities?

Yeah, I did. I was with the band and Mr. Grant. Mr. Grant was a wonderful man, and I wanted . . . well, anyway, I wanted to play cello, and my mother came one day and I‘m on the stage with the band. See, at that time you don‘t have pants. You know, you had a skirt, right.
Yes. So mother said, ―Oh, Mr. Grant, she can‘t play.‖ So, well, it was kind of a drag, you know.
No, couldn‘t play the cello because, you know . . .
You couldn‘t sit right the way . . .
You straddled the cello in a dress, right. [laughs]
Right. But I played viola. It was good. I still have it here.
How long did you play viola?
Just about two years. You know, you had to . . . got to play the piano, and viola kind of fools with you.
